operation_details.item: The user must avoid pseudoephedrine-containing oral decongestants per clinician guidance due to blood pressure concerns.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Hi there! I know you're in the middle of campaign season. How can I help you today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Honestly, this busy week has caught up with me—my head is stuffy and I feel like I'm moving in slow motion.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds rough, especially with deadlines. Are you having other symptoms like aches or a sore throat, or is it mainly congestion?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Mainly congestion and pressure in my sinuses. I'd love something that works fast so I can focus on the campaign launch.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. Before suggesting anything, do you have any restrictions or allergies I should keep in mind?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, actually—A clinician advised me to avoid oral decongestants containing pseudoephedrine because they raise my blood pressure; do not recommend them as a default cold or allergy remedy.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Thank you for telling me—I'll be sure not to suggest pseudoephedrine-based decongestants. I'm not a clinician, so I won't diagnose or prescribe, but I can share supportive options and recommend checking with a pharmacist or your doctor.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That would be great. What can I do to clear my head without those decongestants?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For quick relief, a saline nasal spray or rinse can help thin mucus, and steam from a warm shower or a bowl of hot water can ease sinus pressure. Staying hydrated and using a humidifier at your desk may also make a difference.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I'll try those. Is there anything over-the-counter that's generally considered safe? Or should I just ask the pharmacist?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: It's safest to ask a pharmacist or your clinician, since any medication decision depends on your health history and blood pressure. They can help you choose an option that fits your needs—I don't want to overstep by recommending a specific product.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Good call. I'll stop by the pharmacy after this meeting. Thanks for keeping my blood pressure in mind.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Of course—your health comes first, and a clear head will help you nail the campaign. Feel better soon!

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks, I appreciate it. Time to conquer this week.
